channel.title: NYC High Life Radio News
channel.description: World briefs and local editorial. Check each story for its source date.

item.title: Haiti’s hunger crisis is projected to deepen
item.description: The IPC estimates that 5.94 million people face crisis-level hunger or worse during September 2026–February 2027. Its projection rises to 6.35 million for March–June 2027. Insecurity, displacement, high food prices and climate shocks are driving the outlook.

item.title: Sudan’s damaged power network puts essential care at risk
item.description: The UN says strikes on Sudan’s energy infrastructure are disrupting water and hospital care. Its nearly $2.9 billion humanitarian appeal was 47% funded on November 4.

item.title: Fighting in eastern Congo is closing classrooms
item.description: The UN reports that fighting in Uvira territory has closed 26 primary schools, affecting nearly 6,000 children. Violence is also displacing families and obstructing aid.

item.title: Climate preparedness faces a major funding shortfall
item.description: UNEP estimates developing countries will need about $305 billion a year for climate adaptation by 2035. Even the ambition to triple international public adaptation finance would cover only 20–29% of estimated needs, the agency says.

item.title: Millions of children remain outside formal education
item.description: UNICEF and UNESCO report that 53% of primary-school-age children in Afghanistan are outside formal general education. Their report also says more than 2.6 million girls have been denied secondary education since 2021.

item.title: Displacement and rising prices squeeze families in Yemen
item.description: The UN reports nearly 310,000 people displaced in Yemen since early August. Disrupted transport has driven up prices in Taiz; many families still need shelter.

item.title: Brooklyn library puts teen creativity on its autumn calendar
item.description: Writing, journaling and seasonal crafts feature in Brooklyn Public Library’s October program ideas for young readers.

item.title: Brooklyn families: bring better questions to the school search
item.description: NYC High Life Radio looks at a Brooklyn Public Library event built around researching public schools.

item.title: Trinidad and Tobago: mathematics moves into the spotlight
item.description: NYC High Life Radio follows the next stage of a secondary-school mathematics competition.

item.title: Saint Lucia cricket: a return worth following
item.description: NYC High Life Radio puts women’s cricket and competitive opportunity in the spotlight.
